metadata.summary: Katie Taylor acclaimed becoming a three-time undisputed world champion in her farewell fight at Croke Park as the most special moment of her decorated career.

Sunday 6 September 2026 08:25, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the fight between Katie Taylor and Flora Pili Katie Taylor acclaimed becoming a three-time undisputed world champion in her farewell fight at Croke Park as the most special moment of her decorated career. Taylor outclassed Flora Pili in a unanimous points victory in front of a crowd of 80,000 to ensure her three decades as an amateur and professional boxer ended in fairytale fashion. Wild celebrations followed the announcement that she had overwhelmed the previously unbeaten Pili 100-90 100-90 98-91 on the scorecards. For Taylor the feeling of signing off in front of her fans bettered winning Olympic gold at London 2012, headlining Madison Square Garden and her trilogy against Amanda Serrano. Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16. The 22-year-old will next face compatriot Iva Jovic for a quarter-final spot. "I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said. messages.text: Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Carty falls through ropes in round one

metadata.summary: Dave Allen's heavyweight clash with Thomas Carty at Croke Park ended in a bizarre no contest after the Irish favourite fell out of the ring during the first round.
metadata.content: David Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Thomas Carty falls through ropes in round one on Katie Taylor undercard | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content David Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Thomas Carty falls through ropes in round one on Katie Taylor undercard Chief support bout for Katie Taylor's farewell fight was over in 82 seconds as Irish favourite, who was expected to win, tumbles through the ropes and is unable to continue; crowd jeered as incident was shown on Croke Park screens Sunday 6 September 2026 07:15, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Carty's fight came to an end during round one against Dave Allen after the fighter fell out of the ring and required medical attention. Dave Allen's heavyweight clash with Thomas Carty at Croke Park ended in a bizarre no contest after the Irish favourite fell out of the ring during the first round. The chief support for Katie Taylor's final fight before retirement was over after just 82 seconds with Carty - seeking the biggest win of his 12-bout career - unable to continue. Allen caught Carty on the back of the head with a clubbing right hand and the Dublin southpaw tumbled through the ropes as much through momentum as the shot itself and onto the floor, where he was laid on his back. messages.text: Taylor dominates Pili in final fight of career at Croke Park

metadata.summary: Katie Taylor bid an emotional farewell to boxing as the Irish icon dominated Flora Pili in the final fight of her storied career at a packed out Croke Park on Saturday.
metadata.content: Katie Taylor wins final fight of boxing career after beating Flora Pili on emotional night at Dublin's Croke Park | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Katie Taylor wins final fight of boxing career after beating Flora Pili on emotional night at Dublin's Croke Park Katie Taylor beats Flora Pili in the final fight of her boxing career, becoming an undisputed world champion for the third time; the judges score it 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 as Taylor headlines first boxing event at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972. Cam Hogwood NFL Journalist @ch_skysports Sunday 6 September 2026 07:17, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the fight between Katie Taylor and Flora Pili Katie Taylor bid an emotional farewell to boxing as the Irish icon dominated Flora Pili in the final fight of her storied career at a packed out Croke Park on Saturday. The 40-year-old stormed to a unanimous decision victory to clinch the vacant WBC super-lightweight belt and bow out as a three-time undisputed world champion with 83,000 fans in attendance at Dublin's historic sporting home. Taylor, an Olympic champion and two-weight undisputed champion, hangs up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest female boxer in history and a game-changing pioneer for women's sport.
